chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who catches the second rak'ah of the prayer with the Imam, and it is his first [rak'ah]; what should he do when the Imam sits? He said: 'He should lean back and not be able to sit comfortably. If the third [rak'ah] is for the Imam and it is his second, let him wait a little when the Imam stands, for the time it takes to recite the Tashahhud, then join the Imam.'

He said: And I asked him about a man who catches the last two rak'ahs of the prayer; what should he do regarding recitation? He said: 'Recite in them, for they are the first two for you, so do not make the beginning of your prayer its end.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a person who joins the congregational prayer late and misses one or two rak'ahs?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the practical mechanics for a latecomer (*mu'tamin*) joining the Imam, distinguishing between catching the first rak'ah (requiring a specific standing posture) and the last two (requiring recitation as they count as the first two). It highlights the Shia juristic principle that the number of rak'ahs caught determines their legal status, ensuring the prayer's validity even when the sequence is disrupted. The narration underscores the importance of maintaining continuity with the Imam while fulfilling individual obligations during the transition.
